Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao

sentences.text:
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5439 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioner/accused No.1 seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.80 of 2018 of Indrapalem Police Station, East Godavari District, which was registered for the offences under Section 270 R/w.34 of IPC and Sections 5 and 22 of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short, 'COTP Act, 2003').
2.

entities.text: Indrapalem Police Station, East Godavari District
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 24.03.2018 at 11.00 A.M., the Sub-Inspector of Police, Indrapalem Police Station along with his staff and mediators, on receiving the credible information, proceeded to D.No.11-18, Lalitha Rice Mill godowns, near Balayogi statue centre, Turangi village, Kakinada rural and found illegal manufacturing of banned tobacco products which is a malignant act likely to spread infection of dangerous disease, seized the manufacturing machineries, chemical and lease agreement deed by the petitioner.
Hence, the FIR is registered for the offence under Section 270 R/w.34 of IPC and Section 5 R/w. 22 of COTP Act, 2003.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, the Gutka which is a tobacco product would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, UDPR,J 'FSS Act') and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.

As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and only quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act, whereas permitted the respondents to proceed against the petitioners therein for the offences punishable under the provisions of COTP Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is partly allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner under Section 270 R/w.34 of IPC is hereby quashed and the respondents are permitted to proceed against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 5 R/w Section 22 of COTP Act.
5. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
